name: Tally

mentions.evidence: ~$501k MRR / $6M ARR (Sep 2026), 2.5M users, team of 10, bootstrapped; 43% of new users via AI search.

whyThisMatters:
You make a Tally form by typing, like a doc. Write a question, drop in a block. If you've used Notion, you already get it. They say you can start one without even making an account.

The free plan is the weird part. Unlimited forms and unlimited submissions, as long as you stay inside the fair-use rules they publish. No "three forms, then paywall." Someone can send a real form to a customer before they ever see a price.

The blocks cover the stuff that usually kicks you into another app. Contact details, a file, a signature, a payment. Same form. They host it in Europe, they say they're GDPR compliant, they don't do cookie tracking, and the answers are encrypted on the way and when they're stored. If your customers are in the EU, that's the line that matters.

It's easy to say out loud. It's a form, but you just type it. That's most of what the site leads with. The paid stuff sits on top of a tool people can already use. Fair use is the only cap on the free plan, and they write the rule down instead of making you book a call to hear it.

People use it for contact forms, applications, quizzes, the usual stuff. The difference they keep coming back to is you don't learn a builder. You write. A payment or a signature is just another block, so the person filling it in doesn't get kicked to another site halfway through.
